faq.a: Because the gain applies to a smaller balance. A $10,000 portfolio that falls 20% is worth $8,000. It needs $2,000 to get back to $10,000, and $2,000 is 25% of $8,000. The formula is loss divided by (1 minus loss).
faq.q: Why does a 20% loss need a 25% gain to recover?

faq.a: It depends on the return you assume. At a steady 7% a year, a 25% gain takes about 3.3 years. Enter any return to see the estimate, but real returns vary every year, so the time is an illustration, not a promise.
No. This is the gain needed on the remaining balance alone. Adding new money would shorten the recovery, but this tool shows the pure math of the loss.
No. It is a steady rate you enter for illustration. Investment returns are never steady, and past returns do not guarantee future results.
